To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“what gets measured is not always what gets managed”.
the statement is a false statement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the management of measurements, rather than the measurement of management.
the importance of communication and the need for a precise understanding of the meaning of management catch‐phases.
the management of measurements and their communication to stakeholders, rather than the management of what gets measured.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
what gets measured gets managed, but only to the extent that it can be measured.
“what gets measured and managed gets managed”.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
what gets measured gets managed, but only when it is done properly, and only when it is communicated effectively.
the measurement of performance must be based on the customer's view of the product or service and not on the view of the internal management.
the measurement of performance must be based on the needs of the external stakeholder and the internal stakeholders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the measurement of an activity is not sufficient to ensure that it is managed in the best interest of the end‐use consumer.
precise communication is a prerequisite to alignment between internal and end‐use stakeholders.
the management of measurements should be aligned with the management of the processes that create them.
